battle.name: 瑞挪戰爭 (1814年)
battle.theater: 奧斯福爾德與波胡斯蘭邊境
battle.brief: 一八一四年七月，瑞典依《基爾條約》要求挪威併入王國，臨時政府與埃爾斯沃爾制憲會議拒絕接受，瑞典王儲貝納多特即自波胡斯蘭越境，沿格洛馬河推進。挪威軍在托弗魯德橋頂住瑞典的正面衝鋒，令進攻停滯，但八月召開的埃爾斯沃爾會議以莫斯公約接受合併。長槍在北歐民兵序列裡只剩近戰象徵與執旗標記。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 一八一四年的瑞挪之戰，是北歐王位與國家歸屬危機演成的一場短促邊境戰爭，交戰方是瑞典王國與它剛剛取得的挪威。背景是丹麥－挪威王國在一八一四年一月十四日的《基爾條約》中被拆分：丹麥把挪威割讓給瑞典，換取瑞典放棄對丹麥德意志屬地的一切要求，這條條約由英國、俄國與普魯士共同擔保。接管挪威的瑞典國王卡爾十三世是一名年幼而缺乏本國政治資本的君主，攝政團與軍方遂把執行條約、讓挪威入伙一事當作凝聚國家的手段；攝政貝納多特本人在一八一四年的對俄戰爭中嶄露頭角，軍方支持他親征挪威。挪威方面的抵抗力量則來自另一個傳統：王室與教會、地主與軍官組成的埃爾斯沃爾制憲會議，主張一八〇九年以後已經建立並在實踐中運作過的挪威國家應當延續下去。挪威在體制上並非一盤散沙：它有自己兩院制的斯托爾提、有省級行政、有常備軍，也有按地方動員的民兵「風暴隊」，常備軍規模不大，卻與瑞典軍同樣裝備火槍與野戰炮，兩軍之間的差別主要在於經驗與後勤，而非裝備。瑞典方面，軍隊以正規步兵與騎兵為骨幹，並在南格蘭、博胡斯蘭等地徵召民兵，輔以沿海分艦隊，在格洛馬河兩岸與峽灣水道取得制水權。外交上這場戰爭還牽涉三方：英國以海上封鎖支援瑞典並向北歐輸出條約安排，俄國雖在條約中擔保人，卻對挪威的戰略價值保持興趣，普魯士則希望北歐保持一個穩定的統一國家。挪威軍隊內部也存在貫穿國界的忠誠：出身挪威而服務於丹麥王室的將領，戰時倒向瑞典的例子並不少見。
countriesEn: The Swedish–Norwegian war of 1814 was a short border war produced by a crisis of kingship and national ownership in northern Europe, fought between the kingdom of Sweden and the Norway it had just acquired. The background was the dismemberment of the Danish–Norwegian monarchy by the Treaty of Kiel of 14 January 1814: Denmark ceded Norway to Sweden in exchange for Swedish renunciation of all claims to Denmark's German possessions, and the treaty was guaranteed by Britain, Russia and Prussia. The king who received Norway, Charles XIII, was a boy without political capital of his own, so the regency council and the army turned the enforcement of the treaty and the incorporation of Norway into a means of rallying the country; the regent Bernadotte had made his name in the war against Russia in 1814, and the military backed his personal command of the Norwegian expedition. The force that resisted came out of another tradition: the Eidsvoll Constituent Assembly, made up of the royal house, the clergy, landowners and officers, held that the Norwegian state which had existed and worked in practice since 1809 ought to be continued. Norway was not without structure: it had its two-chamber Storting, its provincial administration, a small standing army and a locally raised militia called the landstorm, and the standing army was equipped with muskets and field guns much like the Swedish. The difference between the two armies lay less in equipment than in experience and logistics. On the Swedish side the army was built on regular infantry and cavalry with militia raised in Sørlandet, Bohuslän and other districts, supported by a coastal squadron that held the waters of the Glomma and the fjord approaches. Three further parties belong to the diplomatic background: Britain backed Sweden with a naval blockade and carried the settlement north, Russia had guaranteed the treaty but kept an eye on Norway's strategic value, and Prussia preferred a stable unified state in the north. Loyalties in the Norwegian army also ran straight across the new border, and officers born in Norway who had served the Danish crown can be found on the Swedish side in this campaign.
people: 挪威方面的核心人物是攝政克里斯蒂安·腓特烈親王。他是丹麥王室的成員，被派來主持挪威事務，在一八一四年二月四日於埃爾斯沃爾宣布挪威脫離丹麥而獨立，四月召開制憲會議，五月十七日通過新憲法；他既是獨立運動的象徵，也是日後接受合併的關鍵人物，一八一四年五月二十二日以辭職化解了國會與攝政團之間的僵局。約翰·斯韋德魯普是制憲會議的主席，後來長期擔任斯托爾提議長，他代表北歐國家主義的務實路線，主張保住挪威自己的憲法、議會與軍隊，最後在莫斯公約上簽字。同時在戰場上決定勝負的是兩位挪威將領：喬治·卡爾斯滕·安克率領第一旅守托弗魯德橋，與瑞典正面硬撼；奧德·伊瓦爾·桑德貝里率第二旅控制高地，幾次側擊把瑞典的攻勢壓回去。瑞典方面，攝政貝納多特是這場戰爭的策動者兼總指揮，國王卡爾十三世年幼，實際上由他與元老院運作；德貝爾恩中將率領前突部隊，是瑞典在格洛馬河上的戰場指揮，屢次強攻未能奏效；此外還有像庫爾特·羅森這樣的跨界人物，他原本是丹麥王室的挪威籍將軍，戰時轉投瑞典並受封伯爵，說明這場戰爭裡國界與忠誠並不重合。挪威的風暴隊則由各地區的射擊隊長與地方首領率領，許多曾在丹麥－挪威海軍或海岸民兵中服役，是夏季短期集結的戰力。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Norwegian side was the regent Prince Christian Frederik, a member of the Danish royal house who was sent to conduct Norwegian affairs. On 4 February 1814 he proclaimed at Eidsvoll that Norway was independent of Denmark; he summoned the Constituent Assembly in April, and on 17 May the new constitution was adopted. He was at once the symbol of the independence movement and the key to its eventual acceptance of union; on 22 May 1814 he resigned, breaking the deadlock between the assembly and the council of state. Johan Sverdrup chaired the Constituent Assembly and later led the Storting for long years. He represented the pragmatic version of the Norwegian national cause, insisting on preserving Norway's own constitution, parliament and army, and he signed the Convention of Moss. On the battlefield two Norwegian commanders settled the outcome: Georg Carsten Anker led the 1st Brigade at the bridge of Toverud and met the Swedish head-on, and Odd Ivar Sandberg held the heights with the 2nd Brigade, striking the Swedish attack back several times. On the Swedish side the regent Bernadotte was the driving force and the overall commander; with the boy king Charles XIII, the real business was done by him and the council of state. General Döbeln led the advance columns and commanded in the field along the Glomma, pressing attacks that never took. There were also figures who crossed the new border: Count Curt von Rosen, a Norwegian-born officer of the Danish crown, went over to Sweden and was ennobled there, showing that in this war frontiers and loyalties did not coincide. The Norwegian landstorm was led by district marksmen and local notables, many of them with service in the Danish–Norwegian navy or the coastal militia, gathered for a single summer's service.
kits: 長槍在一八一四年的北歐幾乎只剩下編制上的痕跡。歐洲本土的長槍兵團在十八世紀已全部廢除，瑞典與丹麥－挪威的步兵在十八世紀末改用燧發滑膛槍與刺刀，長槍僅在少數單位以士官執握的杆兵器形式存在，用於執旗、標定陣形與儀式；真正與它同源的近戰兵器，是北歐民兵體系裡為數可觀的長矛——在火槍不足的民兵連裡，長矛讓沒有槍的人也能站住陣腳，維持住線陣的完整。作戰裝備方面，挪威軍以燧發滑膛步槍為主，騎兵極少，只有數個騎兵連，配少量卡賓槍與手槍，炮兵是連屬三磅與六磅滑膛炮以及幾門更舊的野戰炮，軍旗採北歐式的長方形旗幟，由連長以上軍官執掌。瑞典方面，步兵用一八〇六年型燧發步槍與刺刀，擲彈兵與輕步兵用較輕的滑膛槍，騎兵是卡賓槍、馬槍與瑞典式輕馬刀，炮兵同樣以三磅、六磅野戰炮為主，另有師屬炮與攻城炮，後勤靠雙輪馬車、牛車與徵用的小船，冬季則靠雪橇。真正決定這場戰爭的裝備其實是地形與季節：格洛馬河與峽灣的冰封直接決定了補給與渡河，春季浮冰使內河航行停擺，冬季結冰則把河面變成可以強行通過的硬路，兩軍的實際部署幾乎全由這件事決定。
kitsEn: The pike in the north in 1814 survives only as a trace in the order of battle. The native European pike regiments had all been abolished during the eighteenth century, and Swedish and Danish-Norwegian infantry had gone over to flintlock smoothbore muskets and bayonets at the end of that century; the pike lingered in a few units only as a polearm carried by sergeants, for the colours, for marking the line and for parade. The genuinely analogous close weapon was the spear, and spears remained numerous in the northern militia system: in militia companies short of muskets the spear let men without guns still hold their place and keep the line intact. As for the fighting equipment, the Norwegian army was armed mainly with flintlock smoothbore muskets; its cavalry was minimal, a few squadrons with carbines and pistols; its artillery was regimental three- and six-pounder smoothbore guns together with a few older pieces; the colours were the northern rectangular type, carried by officers from company commander upward. On the Swedish side the infantry used the 1806 pattern flintlock musket and the bayonet, grenadiers and light troops carried lighter smoothbore guns, the cavalry had carbines, horse pistols and the light Swedish sabre, and the artillery was again built on three- and six-pounder smoothbore guns, with brigade guns and siege pieces above them; the rear areas relied on two-wheeled carts, ox wagons and requisitioned boats, and on sledges in winter. The equipment that truly shaped this war was terrain and season. The ice on the Glomma and on the fjord approaches determined supply and crossing: the drifting ice of spring stopped inland navigation, while the hard ice of winter turned the rivers into roads that could be forced, and the actual dispositions of both armies were decided by that fact rather than by anything in the armoury.
tactics: 瑞典軍的戰術是典型的北歐冬季邊界戰役樣式：以縱隊沿單一的陸路走廊直插縱深，同時以艦隊在沿海切斷對手的活動範圍。七月初，軍隊自波胡斯蘭方向越過斯文松邊境，沿一條狹窄的內陸道路直撲奧斯福爾德，前哨戰的結果是瑞典分隊越過格洛馬河佔領數處渡口，但主攻方向選擇了托弗魯德這座唯一有橋樑的渡口。七月十八日夜，德貝爾恩的前突縱隊在暴雨中逼近橋頭，試圖以夜襲奪取北岸；挪威第一旅在安克率領下踞守橋堍與北岸高地，以火槍齊射與刺刀反擊，把瑞典的正面衝鋒壓回南岸，桑德貝里的第二旅則從側翼高地上往下壓，幾次把爬上來的瑞典縱隊趕回橋南。挪威方面的戰術要點是以地形換時間：用一座橋、一條渡口和兩片高地拖住敵人的縱深，等待對方的政治條件成熟。瑞典在托弗魯德受阻之後轉向海岸，佔領哈爾登並以分艦隊封鎖挪威沿岸，弗雷德里克斯塔一度被圍，城池最終選擇開城。就在這段軍事僵持之中，挪威的政治層面發生轉變：七月一日斯托爾提與攝政團決定抵抗，八月十四日在莫斯召開的會議上決定接受合併，戰爭於是以外交方式收場，而托弗魯德阻擊戰的意義正在於它把雙方的談判籌碼從桌面換到了戰場。
tacticsEn: The Swedish method was the classic northern winter border campaign: columns pushed along a single corridor of roads into the interior, with a squadron at sea meanwhile shutting the opponent's room to manoeuvre. In early July the troops crossed the Svinesund border from Bohuslän and drove along one narrow inland road towards Østfold; the outposts produced a Swedish detachment across the Glomma at several fords, but the main effort was directed at Toverud, the one crossing with a bridge. On the night of 18 July Döbeln's leading column closed on the bridge head in pouring rain, attempting a night seizure of the north bank. Anker's 1st Brigade, dug in on the bridgehead and the heights beyond, answered with musketry volleys and the bayonet and threw the Swedish assault back south of the river, while Sandberg's 2nd Brigade came down from the heights on the flank and drove off the columns that had climbed the slope. The Norwegian tactical point was to buy time with ground: one bridge, one ford and two plateaus were enough to hold the Swedish in depth until the political conditions ripened. After the check at Toverud the Swedish turned to the coast, occupied Halden and closed the Norwegian shore with the squadron; Fredrikstad was besieged for a time and eventually opened its gates. It was in that military stalemate that the Norwegian political position turned: on 1 July the Storting and the council of state resolved on resistance, and at the meeting at Moss on 14 August decided on union. The war thus ended diplomatically, and the significance of the stand at Toverud lay precisely in the fact that it converted the terms of negotiation from a matter of paper into a matter of the field.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。《基爾條約》訂於一八一四年一月十四日；挪威宣獨立在二月四日；埃爾斯沃爾制憲會議四月召開，新憲法五月十七日通過；七月初瑞典軍越境，托弗魯德之戰在七月十九日；莫斯公約簽於八月十四日；貝納多特於九月七日被選為挪威國王，十一月十七日宣誓就位。兵員方面，挪威常備軍規模在數千人，各地方風暴隊與民兵合計可集結的兵力在五千至一萬之間；瑞典方面投入的正規軍與民兵合計在數萬之譜，常見估計自兩萬餘至四萬不等。托弗魯德一役，挪威守橋的第一旅約一千人上下，第二旅與民兵另在側翼，瑞典投入的攻擊縱隊為數千人；挪威方面的陣亡與受傷約數百人，瑞典方面的損失也以數百人計，具體數目各史料說法不一。距離上，瑞典軍自波胡斯蘭越境處到托弗魯德約一百餘公里，格洛馬河全程近兩百公里，軍隊只能沿河谷一條道路行進，這一點在冬季結冰時既是優勢也是陷阱。挪威全國人口在當時約八十餘萬，兵員比例與平時的民兵徵召率則因地區而異。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The Treaty of Kiel was signed on 14 January 1814; Norwegian independence was proclaimed on 4 February; the Constituent Assembly met from April and the new constitution was adopted on 17 May; the Swedish crossed the border in early July, the battle of Toverud was fought on 19 July, the Convention of Moss was signed on 14 August, Bernadotte was elected king of Norway on 7 September and took the oath on 17 November. On men: Norway's standing army numbered some thousands, and its landstorm and militia together could be assembled to between five and ten thousand; the Swedish committed regulars and militia numbering in the tens of thousands, common estimates running from a little over twenty thousand to forty thousand. At Toverud the Norwegian 1st Brigade holding the bridge was of the order of a thousand men, with Sandberg's 2nd Brigade and the militia out on the flank, against several thousand Swedish in the attacking columns; Norwegian dead and wounded ran to several hundred, Swedish losses likewise in the hundreds, with the exact figures given differently by different sources. As to distance, the Swedish march from the border crossing in Bohuslän to Toverud was of the order of a hundred and some kilometres, the Glomma itself runs close to two hundred kilometres, and the troops could only move along the single road in the valley — a fact that was an advantage under the winter ice and a trap at the same time. Norway's population stood at rather more than eight hundred thousand, and the ratio of men to population varied widely with the local rate of militia levy.
cause: 打起來的原因，可以分成三層。最直接的一層是《基爾條約》本身的結果：一八一四年一月的條約把挪威判給瑞典，但沒有問過挪威人。丹麥－挪威王國自一八〇七年以來先後遭到英國的炮擊與丹麥的挫敗，一八〇八至一八〇九年的丹麥戰爭中瑞典一度陳兵於挪威境內，挪威人對瑞典並無敵意，只是習慣了丹麥的市場、海軍與制度；條約把這份習慣突然作廢，自然激起反抗。第二層是挪威內部的利益計算：北方貴族、教會與軍官擔心一旦併入瑞典，挪威將失去獨立的海軍與外交地位，木材與鐵的出口條件也會被重新談判；這些人願意接受一位瑞典國王，卻不肯接受一份由瑞典代擬的憲法。於是有了埃爾斯沃爾：一八一四年五月的制憲會議把丹麥的憲政形式整體搬過來，只改掉君主與選舉的關鍵條文，把國會的權限寫得比丹麥時期更硬。第三層是瑞典自己的算計。卡爾十三世的王位來自一九一四年式的宮廷政變，貝納多特攝政團的權力仍不穩固，瑞典需要一場對外勝利來凝聚這個新王朝；北方的木鐵礦產是戰時經濟的支柱，戰後的和平卻意味著軍費與造船業的收縮；此外俄國在條約中擔保人卻對北歐的戰略位置頗有興趣，瑞典不能容忍出現一個受俄國影響的獨立挪威。英國的態度是把這件事當作條約體系的一環，用封鎖支持瑞典，等於替挪威的政治抵抗加了一道枷。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause. The most immediate was the plain result of the Treaty of Kiel: the treaty of January 1814 assigned Norway to Sweden without asking the Norwegians. The Danish–Norwegian monarchy had suffered British bombardment in 1807 and Danish defeat in the war of 1808–1809, during which Swedish troops stood inside Norway for a time, and the Norwegians bore no hostility towards Sweden — they were merely used to Danish markets, a Danish navy and Danish institutions. The treaty abruptly voided that habit, and the reaction was immediate. The second layer was the interest calculation inside Norway: the northern aristocracy, the clergy and the officers feared that absorption by Sweden would cost Norway its own fleet and its diplomatic standing, and that the conditions for exporting timber and iron would be renegotiated from scratch. They were prepared to accept a Swedish king; they were not prepared to accept a constitution drafted for them by Sweden. Hence Eidsvoll: the assembly of May 1814 carried over the Danish constitutional form almost entire, changing only the clauses that touched the monarch and the election, and writing the powers of the parliament harder than they had been under Denmark. The third layer was Sweden's own arithmetic. Charles XIII had come to the throne by a palace revolution, the authority of Bernadotte's regency was still unsettled, and Sweden needed a foreign victory to rally the new dynasty. Northern timber and iron underpinned the war economy, while peace meant shrinking military expenditure and shipbuilding. And Russia, having guaranteed the treaty, had an evident interest in the strategic position of the north, so Sweden could not tolerate an independent Norway under Russian influence. Britain's attitude was to treat the affair as part of the settlement, supporting Sweden with a blockade — which in effect tightened the noose around the Norwegian political resistance.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果，是北歐四分之一土地的政治歸屬被一次戰役決定，而不是被議會慢慢談成。挪威以自己的憲法加入了瑞典，卻保留了自己的斯托爾提、國務會議與省級行政，一八一四年五月十七日的憲法在挪威一直有效到一九〇五年，而且至今仍是挪威現行憲法——這在歐洲是獨一份。軍事上，兩點被記住：一是守一條河、一座橋、一片高地可以拖住一支優勢兵力的縱隊，二是民兵的徵召與訓練決定了國家的底線。托弗魯德阻擊戰在挪威的軍事傳統裡留下了具體的名字，兩個旅的指揮官安克與桑德貝里成為國家記憶中的人物，一八〇〇年代挪威軍官以瑞典軍人身分延續的傳統也由此形成。政治上，這次合併製造了一個長期未解的矛盾：一八一四年五月十七日的憲法前言明確宣稱挪威人民是一個獨立的民族，卻在同一天把國家主權交給瑞典王，兩者之間的落差在此後九十年裡不斷被提出來，成為一八八〇年代議會衝突的根源，最終在一九〇五年的_union dissolution 中爆發。經濟上，挪威得到長期的和平與較寬鬆的財政狀況，也得到木材與鐵的新市場，卻失去獨立的海軍與外交的主導權，丹麥－挪威王國就此徹底解體，北歐的權力中心北移，瑞典從此成為波羅的海的主要國家。
impactEn: The immediate result was that a quarter of northern Europe changed political ownership by force of arms rather than by slow parliamentary negotiation. Norway joined Sweden with its own constitution, but kept its Storting, its council of state and its provincial administration, and the constitution of 17 May 1814 remained in force in Norway until 1905 and is still Norway's constitution today — a unique case in Europe. Militarily two lessons were recorded: a single river, a single bridge and a stretch of high ground can hold a superior enemy in depth; and the muster and training of the militia decide a country's floor. The stand at Toverud left specific names in the Norwegian military tradition, and the two brigade commanders, Anker and Sandberg, became figures in the national memory; the practice of Norwegian officers serving in Swedish units from the 1800s onward grew out of the same settlement. Politically the union created a contradiction that would not resolve for ninety years. The preamble of the constitution of 17 May 1814 declared the Norwegian people a distinct nation, while the same document handed state sovereignty to a Swedish king; the gap between the two was raised again and again in the following decades, became the root of the parliamentary conflicts of the 1880s, and finally erupted in the dissolution of the union in 1905. Economically Norway gained a long period of peace and comparatively sound public finances, and new markets for timber and iron, but lost an independent navy and any real say in its own foreign policy; the Danish–Norwegian monarchy was thereby broken up for good and the centre of power in the north shifted to Sweden, which from then on was the principal Baltic power.
result: 一八一四年七月到八月，戰爭以挪威接受合併告終。軍事上，挪威在托弗魯德擊退瑞典的正面攻勢，延緩了瑞典的推進，換來了幾個星期的談判時間；瑞典在占領哈爾登、封鎖沿岸之後，於八月十四日在莫斯召開的會議上與挪威攝政團達成協議：挪威不再抵抗，但保留一八一四年五月十七日的憲法與斯托爾提，國王問題留待全體斯托爾提決定。九月七日，貝納多特當選挪威國王，十一月十七日宣誓就位；同年十一月十日簽訂的聯合條約進一步規定共戴一位君主、各自保有軍隊與海軍，並設立共同的聯合機構。一八一五年春天的斯托爾提以絕大多數決議保留了一八一四年的憲法，只作了小幅修改。於是挪威在主權上併入瑞典，在制度上保持了自己：這份安排維持了整整九十一年，直到一九〇五年聯合體制崩解、挪威重新宣示獨立。回頭看，這場戰爭裡真正被決定的是挪威國家的形式而非其存亡——它的憲法、議會與軍隊在戰後被完整保留下來，使北歐出現了一個在同一個君主之下長期維持兩套憲政的罕見安排。
resultEn: From July to August 1814 the war ended with Norway accepting union. Militarily the Norwegian stand at Toverud threw back the Swedish frontal assault and bought the weeks of time that the negotiations needed; after the occupation of Halden and the blockade of the coast, the meeting at Moss on 14 August reached agreement with the Norwegian council of state: Norway would no longer resist, but the constitution of 17 May 1814 and the Storting were to be kept, and the question of the king was left to a full Storting. On 7 September Bernadotte was elected king of Norway and took the oath on 17 November; the Union Treaty of 10 November that year went further, laying down a shared monarch, separate armies and navies, and a joint union council. In the spring of 1815 the Storting decided by a large majority to retain the constitution of 1814 with only slight amendments. Norway was thus merged into Sweden in sovereignty while keeping its own institutions to itself: the arrangement stood for ninety-one years, until the union collapsed in 1905 and Norway reasserted its independence. Looking back, what the war actually settled was the form of the Norwegian state rather than its survival — its constitution, its parliament and its army were preserved intact after the fighting, and northern Europe was left with the rare arrangement of two constitutional systems enduring for a long time under one monarch.
